name: The Content Engine: 12 Solo Founder Prompts
tagline: Turn a single idea into a full week of high-converting social media posts in minutes.
metaDescription: Stop staring at a blank screen. Use these 12 practical, plug-and-play AI prompts to transform one core idea into a week of engaging posts for solo founders.
description:
Running a startup alone leaves zero time for endless brainstorming and content creation. If you are a solo founder struggling to stay visible online, this prompt pack is built specifically for you. The Content Engine solves the classic 'blank page' syndrome by giving you a systematic, repeatable framework to scale one idea across multiple platforms and formats without sounding generic. 

These prompts work because they are engineered to extract your unique product insights, customer pain points, and industry opinions rather than spitting out fluffy, AI-sounding platitudes. Each prompt includes a specific usage tip to ensure the output matches your brand voice and target audience. Whether you are building in public on X, sharing deep dives on LinkedIn, or nurturing an email list, these plug-and-play workflows save you hours every single week. Simply feed the prompt your raw thought, apply the usage tip, and watch a week of cohesive content generate instantly.
includes: 1 PDF guide with 12 plug-and-play AI prompts
1 Notion template database containing all prompts and usage tips
Categories include: Threads, Contrarian Takes, Case Studies, and Engagement
sampleItems: Take our core product feature: [Feature Name]. Draft a 5-part X/Twitter thread explaining the hidden problem this feature solves, aimed at [Target Audience] who are tired of manual work.

Act as a direct-response copywriter. Take this raw insight: [Raw Idea]. Write a short, punchy LinkedIn post starting with a contrarian take that challenges common industry advice in the [Your Niche] space.

items.title: The Contrarian Hook
items.body: Act as a direct-response copywriter. Take this conventional industry belief: [Insert Belief]. Write a short, punchy LinkedIn post that challenges this belief using a contrarian take from our startup's perspective. Start with a bold 3-word hook, explain why the old way is failing solo founders, and end with a soft question to drive comments. Keep the tone pragmatic, direct, and free of corporate jargon. Aim for under 150 words to maximize mobile readability.

items.title: The Feature-to-Benefit Thread
items.body: Take our product feature: [Insert Feature] and translate it into a 5-part X/Twitter thread for [Target Audience]. Tweet 1: Hook the reader by highlighting a painful manual workflow they currently tolerate. Tweet 2: Introduce our feature as the exact antidote. Tweets 3-4: Break down two specific use cases with quick implementation steps. Tweet 5: Call to action inviting them to test the product. Ensure each tweet flows naturally into the next without fluff.

items.title: The Build-in-Public Milestone
items.body: Act as an honest startup founder sharing behind-the-scenes metrics. Take this recent event or metric: [Insert Metric/Event]. Write a transparent build-in-public post for X/Twitter. Share what went right, what completely broke, and the single most important lesson learned. Avoid toxic positivity; keep it grounded and useful for other bootstrap founders on a similar journey. End with an open invitation for advice.

items.title: The Customer Pain Point Story
items.body: Write a short narrative post for LinkedIn detailing a specific frustration our ideal customer faces regarding [Insert Pain Point]. Structure the story using the PAS framework: Problem (describe the daily friction), Agitation (the compounding cost of ignoring it), and Solution (how our product quietly fixes it in the background). Maintain an empathetic yet authoritative voice that positions our software as the reliable helper.

items.title: The Quick Win Tutorial
items.body: Draft a short, highly actionable how-to section for our weekly founder newsletter. Take this quick win: [Insert Actionable Tip]. Explain the step-by-step execution in under 200 words so a busy reader can implement it during their morning coffee. Include clear subheadings and avoid unnecessary preamble. The goal is to deliver immediate utility that makes them look forward to every edition.

items.title: The FAQ Objection Crusher
items.body: Take the most common customer objection we hear on sales calls: [Insert Objection]. Write a LinkedIn post addressing it head-on with total transparency. Acknowledge why the skepticism is completely fair, explain how we designed our product architecture or pricing to solve it, and provide social proof or logic to back it up. End by lowering the barrier to entry for cautious buyers.

items.title: The Micro-Case Study
items.body: Format a quick micro-case study for X/Twitter based on this user success story: [Insert Result/Quote]. Use a simple Before/After structure. Before: The manual chaos the user dealt with. After: The exact metric or time saved after using our tool for [Timeframe]. Keep sentences short, punchy, and highlight real numbers to build instant trust with prospective users.

items.title: The Hot Take Poll Setup
items.body: Create an engaging poll question for LinkedIn or X/Twitter about this industry debate: [Insert Topic]. Write a 2-sentence context hook outlining two contrasting approaches founders take, followed by 4 distinct poll options. Include a short follow-up prompt to drop in the comments immediately after posting to spark a lively debate among niche peers.

items.title: The Resource Roundup
items.body: Compile a curated list of 3 underrated tools, articles, or mental models that help solo founders master [Insert Skill]. Write a 2-sentence blurb for each item explaining exactly why it is worth their time, focusing on practical ROI rather than hype. Keep the formatting clean with bullet points for easy scanning.

items.title: The Founder Vulnerability Post
items.body: Write a grounded reflection post about a recent mistake or failed experiment in our startup journey regarding [Insert Mistake]. Focus heavily on the tactical lesson learned rather than seeking sympathy. Explain how this failure changed our product roadmap or operational strategy. Solo founders respect honesty over perfection—make this authentic and relatable.

items.title: The Vision & Roadmap Share
items.body: Take our upcoming product release or feature update: [Insert Upcoming Feature]. Write an exciting, forward-looking post for X/Twitter explaining why we are building it and who it is specifically for. Invite early feedback from users by asking them to reply with their biggest wishlist item for this specific workflow.

items.title: The Direct Sales Hook
items.body: Write a high-converting, non-sleazy promotional post for LinkedIn offering a direct trial of our product. Hook the reader with a stark comparison between the hard way of doing [Insert Task] versus using our automated software. Clearly state who the product is NOT for to filter out bad leads, and give a crystal-clear call to action pointing to our sign-up page.
